svg.text: 6-mic test array on one breadboard (top view): 4 front + 2 back, shoulders later
Full-size breadboard (63 columns) · XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense · firmware eight_mic_stream · viewer tools/mic_test_ui.py · top of page = front of the wearer
Wires (each column of 5 holes is one strip; any free hole in the strip works)
XIAO 3V3 → top + rail → bridged to bottom + rail; each mic's 3V → nearest + rail
XIAO GND → top − rail → bridged to bottom − rail; each mic's GND → nearest − rail
XIAO D0 → F4, F3 → chained to F5, F2 → down to B4, B1 (all 6 mics)
data line 2: B1 (ch5), S_R joins later (ch4)
data line 3: B4 (ch7), S_L joins later (ch6)
short jumper: to the GND strip next door (ch odd) or 2 over to 3V (ch even)
• Back mics are turned 180°, so their pin order is reversed:
DAT CLK SEL GND 3V from left to right. Follow the printed labels.
• Each SEL goes to exactly one rail. Never join two SEL pins.
• Add one mic at a time and check it in mic_test_ui before the next.
Adding the shoulders later (no other rewiring)
• S_R: 3V, GND, CLK like B1; DAT into B1's DAT strip (col 57);
• S_L: same, DAT into B4's DAT strip (col 3); SEL to 3V3 → ch6.
• Long breadboards often split the rails in the middle: bridge them.
• MEMS mics hear all around; on a bare breadboard, front vs back
differ by spacing, not by facing. A card or foam wall between
the rows mimics the body shadow of the shirt.
• Spacing is shorter than on the shirt (front 5 → 4.6 cm,
back 30 → 13.7 cm). Measure port-to-port for the software.
